key_features.classic_presentation: Ruptured ovarian cyst presents with sudden-onset sharp lower abdominal/pelvic pain, often unilateral. Pain often occurs mid-cycle or with ovulation. Usually self-limited, resolves in hours to days. Large hemorrhagic cysts can cause more significant bleeding.
key_features.typical_demographics: Women of reproductive age. Functional cysts common with normal ovulation.
key_features.pathophysiology_brief: Rupture of physiologic or pathologic ovarian cyst releases fluid into pelvis causing peritoneal irritation.

diagnostic_questions.context: Sudden onset at time of rupture.
Simple ruptured cysts improve over hours. Worsening pain suggests other diagnosis.

red_flags.action: Possible significant hemorrhage - needs urgent evaluation

typical_management: Supportive care, pain control. Most resolve spontaneously. Large hemorrhagic cysts may need observation or rarely surgery.
disposition: Mild: outpatient. Severe pain or hemodynamic changes: ER evaluation.
patient_education: Ovarian cysts are common fluid-filled sacs. When they rupture, they cause temporary pain that usually resolves on its own. Most don't require treatment.
